topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the core learning outcomes concerning cancer etiology.

topics.label: Principles of Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Microenvironment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: They explore how endogenous biological errors, inherited predispositions, environmental exposures, and epidemiological trends interact to drive cancer.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how biological agents and co-infections contribute to oncogenesis, highlighted by the mechanistic case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how distinct dietary, environmental, and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Inflammatory Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how non-mutagenic substances promote tumor growth through chronic inflammation and intracellular signaling pathways.

topics.label: Developmental Timing and Target Cell Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how cellular proliferative states and specific life stages alter susceptibility to carcinogenic exposure.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Assessing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: They review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine and quantify carcinogenicity.
